title: Cohomology properties of maps in (Cat) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (Pursuing Stacks / 'modelizers' circle, ca. 1983 and after). W is a basic localizer on (Cat). For a small category A, A^ is the category of presheaves on A, i_A : A^ -> (Cat) sends X to the category of elements A/X, and W_A = i_A^{-1}(W). The previous page lists four conditions on A: (i) A is totally W-aspherical (A is W-aspherical and products a x b of representables are W-aspherical); (ii) W_A is stable under finite products; (iii) A^ -> Hot_A commutes with finite products; (iv) A^ -> Hot(W) commutes with finite products. There Grothendieck proves that (i) and (iv) are equivalent, using (A/X x Y)/alpha ≃ A/(a x b). He also proves that (i) implies (ii) and that (ii) and (iii) are equivalent.

This page has three parts.

(1) NB on sums. Condition (ii) is visibly stable under sums: if A is the disjoint union of the A_alpha, then A^ is the product of the A_alpha^ and W_A is the product of the W_{A_alpha}. Condition (i) is not stable under sums, since a non-connected category is not aspherical. Hence the implication (i) ⇒ (ii) is strict.

(2) The refined question, and a counterexample. If A satisfies (ii) and is connected, must A be W-aspherical? Answer: no. Take A a group, or a connected groupoid, and W the usual weak equivalences. A^ is then the category of G-sets, and A/X is the action groupoid X//G. A weak equivalence of groupoids is an equivalence of groupoids. A G-map inducing such an equivalence must be bijective on orbits and an isomorphism on stabilizers, hence bijective. So W_A consists of isomorphisms only, and is trivially stable under finite products. But BG is a K(G,1), not contractible, for G ≠ 1. So connectedness plus (ii) does not give asphericity.

(3) Products in (Cat). The finite-product argument works directly in (Cat): a finite product of functors in W is in W, so (Cat) -> Hot(W) commutes with finite products. For infinite products one must show two things:
- an arbitrary product of maps in W lies in W;
- the same holds in A^ (Grothendieck says the second implies the first).
He says that even for the usual weak equivalences W_0 this is not evident to him. The next page asks whether an infinite product of W-aspherical objects is W-aspherical, and judges this as important as the question of infinite sums.
errors: Not an error of Grothendieck's but of the machine transcription: in the NB the condition that fails to be stable under sums must be (i), not (ii); otherwise the sentence is self-contradictory.

The groupoid counterexample is correct for W = usual weak equivalences. Grothendieck states 'W_A consists only of isos' without proof. The short argument is: equivalence of action groupoids means bijection on orbits plus isomorphism on stabilizers, which forces bijectivity. For a general basic localizer W, W restricted to groupoids could be coarser, so the example is specific to W_0 (he says so explicitly).
The parenthetical claim that stability of infinite products in A^ implies it in (Cat) is plausible (e.g. via A = a test category and i_A / Sd-type comparison) but is not justified on the page.

ideas.what: Hierarchy of product conditions on A relative to a basic localizer: totally aspherical vs W_A stable under finite products vs A^ -> Hot commuting with finite products
ideas.modern_name: Totally W-aspherical small categories; compatibility of the localization A^ -> Hot_A with finite products
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Pursuing Stacks), developed by Maltsiniotis (Astérisque 301, 2005) and Cisinski (Astérisque 308, 2006)
ideas.where_published: Pursuing Stacks (sections on test categories, total asphericity, and products)

ideas.what: Condition 'W_A stable under finite products' is stable under sums of categories while total asphericity is not; hence the implication is strict
ideas.modern_name: Stability of local properties under coproducts of small categories

ideas.what: Counterexample: a connected groupoid (group G) has W_A = isomorphisms (for usual weak equivalences), so W_A is product-stable although BG is not aspherical
ideas.modern_name: Action groupoids of G-sets; equivariant maps inducing equivalences of action groupoids are isomorphisms

ideas.what: Every basic localizer is stable under finite products, so (Cat) -> Hot(W) commutes with finite products
ideas.modern_name: Stability of basic localizers under finite products
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Pursuing Stacks / Les Dérivateurs); proofs in Maltsiniotis 2005, Cisinski 2004/2006

ideas.what: Question: are arbitrary (infinite) products of W-equivalences, or of W-aspherical categories, again in W, already for W_0?
ideas.modern_name: Stability of weak homotopy equivalences under infinite products
ideas.usually_credited_to: For W_0 I believe it is now textbook (e.g. treated in Lurie's Kerodon), but I am unsure of the exact reference; for general basic localizers unsure

missed.claim: Grothendieck raises, as being as important as infinite sums, the question of whether arbitrary products of maps in a basic localizer W (or of W-aspherical categories) stay in W. He also notes that stability in presheaf categories A^ would imply stability in (Cat). For W_0 the answer is now standard. For an arbitrary basic localizer I do not know a systematic treatment: which basic localizers are stable under infinite products, and whether the minimal one or those generated by a set have this property.
missed.quote: Pour le cas des produits infinis, il faut voir qu'un produit déf[?] de W est dans W, et/ou itou dans un Â (le deuxième impliquera le premier). Déjà pour l'équiv. faible habituelle W_0, ça ne m'est pas évident.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Infinite-product stability is relevant to the derivator Hot(W) having good infinite limits, i.e. products being homotopy products. Characterizing basic localizers by this property could be a small but genuine addition to Cisinski–Maltsiniotis theory; it may already be implicit there (unsure).

deep.surprise_reason: Routine bookkeeping within the well-documented test-category / basic-localizer theory. The groupoid counterexample is simple, and the infinite-product question is natural and largely answered for W_0. Only the general-W version is mildly open-ended.
transcription_corrections: 'mais la condition (ii) non' should read 'mais la condition (i) non' (total asphericity is what fails for sums).
'est elle W-asphérique (ou itou W-asphérique[?])' is likely 'est-elle W-asphérique (ou tot. W-asphérique)?'.
'dont les A^[?] W_A est formé des seuls iso' should read roughly 'alors W_A est formé des seuls iso (car W est l'équiv. faible habituelle), donc stable par produits finis'.
'puisqu'un tel[?] produit ... conditions[?] finis de fonctions[?] ∈ W est ∈ W' should read roughly 'puisqu'on sait qu'un produit fini de foncteurs ∈ W est ∈ W'.
'un produit déf[?]' is perhaps 'un produit infini' or 'défini'; unclear in image.
